draft_key_information_units.information: Eleving Group achieved record financial performance in 2024 with revenue of EUR 216.6 mln (up 14.5% YoY), EBITDA of EUR 89.8 mln (up 16.1% YoY), net profit of EUR 29.6 mln (up 20.7% YoY and the highest in company history), and a vehicle and consumer financing net portfolio of EUR 371.2 mln (up 16.0% YoY).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report '2024 at a glance' (page 3) and Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss (page 13) show revenue, EBITDA, net profit, and portfolio figures. The text states 'All-time best annual net profit - EUR 29.6 mln' and provides comparative figures for 2021-2024.

draft_key_information_units.information: Key performance drivers included the EUR 29.0 mln equity raised via October 2024 IPO (largest in Nasdaq Riga's history), digital transformation in Europe that nearly doubled application volumes, integration of Sub-Saharan operations (acquired in 2023) that tripled combined portfolio size in the region, and financing of nearly 2,000 electric motorcycles saving ~1,000 metric tonnes of CO2.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Keynote from the CEO (page 4) details the IPO, digitalization, Sub-Saharan integration, and electric mobility achievements. The Unaudited sustainability statement (page 81) confirms the electric motorcycle financing volume and CO2 impact.

draft_key_information_units.information: Segment-wise growth was strongest in Europe (notably Romania, Latvia, and Uzbekistan under Eleving Stella), Africa & Asia (Kenya and Uganda under Eleving Solis with traditional vehicle financing), and consumer finance expansion in Albania, Namibia, and Zambia, driving organic demand and new market entries.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Note 46 (Segment information, pages 68-69) breaks down segment performance and growth drivers. The Management report (page 90) highlights regional contributions to portfolio growth.

draft_key_information_units.information: The capital structure strengthened post-IPO, with equity rising to EUR 108.1 mln (from EUR 65.4 mln in 2023) and a capitalization ratio improving to 29.3% (from 26.1% in 2023), providing ample headroom for future growth while managing EUR 339.6 mln of total borrowings (EUR 72.0 mln due within 12 months).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity (page 16) shows equity movement. Note 35 (Borrowings, page 56) details debt maturity profiles. Alternative Performance Measures (page 70) reports the capitalization ratio.

draft_key_information_units.information: Strategic priorities for 2025-2026 focus on deepening existing markets (Europe and Africa), broadening product portfolios (including electric mobility and consumer finance), and entering new geographies, with a target to nearly double the business size within two years.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Keynote from the CEO (page 5) and Business outlook (page 132) outline the three-pillar strategy and growth ambition. The Management report (page 90) emphasizes digital transformation and product expansion.

draft_key_information_units.information: Material post-reporting events include a March 2025 public bond tap issuing EUR 40 mln of senior secured bonds (maturing 2028) at improved yields and a EUR 1.151 mln refund from North Macedonia related to a contested solidarity tax payment.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Note 47 (Events after balance sheet date, page 70) details the bond offering and tax refund. The Romanian VAT audit outcome (Note 15, page 45) provides context for tax-related developments.

draft_key_information_units.information: The first-time reporting of greenhouse gas emissions showed total scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions of 309,927 tCO2eq, primarily from the financed vehicle fleet, with initiatives underway to reduce emissions intensity (e.g., electric motorcycle financing and hybrid vehicle promotion).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Unaudited sustainability statement (pages 102-110) presents GHG emissions data, methodology, and reduction targets aligned with the ESG framework 2022-2025.

evaluation.selection_rationale: The units prioritize headline financial performance (D1), major YoY changes and key drivers (D2-D4), strategic direction (D5), and material post-period events (D6-D7). Excluded are routine boilerplate items (governance details, remuneration policies, generic risk lists, accounting policies) per the instructions. Each unit represents an independently omittable material theme, with all factual details directly supported by the SOURCE FINANCIAL REPORT. The REFERENCE SUMMARY informed salience weighting but was not used as exhaustive ground truth.
